summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, GERD, and anxiety presented with five days of persistent epigastric discomfort radiating to the throat, accompanied by bothersome belching. The symptoms began after she stopped taking Prilosec due to financial constraints and consumed a large, greasy meal with beer. In the ED, her cardiac workup—including ECG and troponin levels—was unremarkable, and her pain resolved with a GI cocktail. She was admitted for further evaluation and management. During her brief hospitalization, her symptoms were attributed to gastroesophageal reflux disease, and her Prilosec dose was increased to 40 mg daily with insurance coverage confirmed. Her cardiac medications were continued unchanged, and she remained stable. She was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider in two to three weeks and to return if concerning symptoms developed.
